#1538. New mum and ex-Lionesses star Mary Earps names baby boy Xander after announcing her partner's secret birth in heartwarming Instagram video

Published: 04:55 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 05:11 EST, 8 November 2026

Euro-winning Lionesses goalkeeper Mary Earps has named her son Xander after becoming a mother for the first time, having revealed this week that her partner has given birth to a baby boy.

Earps, 33, was a hero of England's Euro 2022 victory at Wembley and starred at the World Cup in 2023, saving a penalty in the final. She won BBC Sports Personality of the Year but later lost her England place to rival Hannah Hampton and retired in acrimonious circumstances.

She moved to France with Paris Saint-Germain but returned to England earlier this year - and has now welcomed her first child with her partner, Kitty Forrest.

'Welcome to the world, Xander,' she posted on Instagram, with a photograph of her newborn's hand.

In a video released on Friday, Earps said: 'I've been keeping a little secret from you all. And I don't think I can talk my way out of this one. So, I think I'm going to have to show you.

'I can't quite believe I'm writing this, but yesterday Kitty and I welcomed our beautiful baby boy into the world!

'We're absolutely over the moon and still trying to take it all in. It's been such an emotional journey getting to this point, and we couldn't be more excited to start this next chapter of our lives as a family of three.'

Mary Earps has revealed the name of her baby boy following his secret birth: Xander

Earps and her partner Kitty (second right) revealed news of welcoming a baby boy (YouTube/Mary Earps)

Earps says she will not be able to take maternity leave due to the rigors of the football season. Her team, London City Lionesses, are eight games into the new Women's Super League season and sit third behind Chelsea and Manchester City.

'I do have one eye sort of on football, which is super weird,' she said.

'In any other job, you would just be like, "Okay, bye. Taking maternity leave, whatever. Um, and you just do what you need to do." But that doesn't really work in football, because you've got games and then, if you take the day off, then you got to think about what that looks like and how that works into sort of your training schedule and the fixture calendar.

'So, it's a little bit more complicated. You can't just take annual leave whenever you want without consequence. You know, it's going to be interesting to see what the next days and weeks bring.'

Earps first revealed that she was in a same-sex relationship in September of last year but largely kept partner Kitty out of the spotlight.

Kitty is a physiotherapist who worked as the lead in her department at Manchester United Women, Earps's former club.

Earps is pictured kissing the trophy after England won Euro 2022 at Wembley Stadium

Earps won BBC Sports Personality of the Year in 2023 following her Euro heroics

In a statement at the time, Earps said: 'I've always tried to keep my personal life separate from my professional one, but it would have felt inauthentic not to include something so important to me in this book. I'm in a really happy relationship.

'The people closest to me have always known, and I feel ready and happy to share that with everyone else now.'

Earps retired from England duty in May last year after the release of her autobiography dragged up a storm with Hampton, the Chelsea goalkeeper who overtook her from understudy to become England No 1.

Earps revealed she told Sarina Wiegman that 'bad behaviour was being rewarded' after Hampton was recalled to the England squad.

#1537. GdS: A start vs. France at San Siro – Cisse’s rapid ascent continues with Mancini’s faith

Alphadjo Cisse continues to go from strength to strength, and his biggest moment yet might be coming during the break.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, beyond the confidence with which he plays and speaks, what’s truly striking is Cisse’s composure in front of goal at just 20 years of age, experiencing his first proper season in the top flight.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

His goal in Genoa seemed easy because he made it so, but it wasn’t. Adrien Rabiot’s pass was quite slow, the distance to the goal wasn’t that close, Genoa were exposed after losing the ball but Bijlow wasn’t in a particularly bad position, and beating him required precision.

Other strikers in those circumstances may have opted for a powerful finish. Not Cisse. He looked for the corner and found it with a lovely precise strike, one which revealed everything about the groove he has found himself in.

It was goal number five in the league for Alphadjo Cisse, making him Milan’s joint-top scorer alongside Rabiot. That extends to eight across all competitions, which puts the young Italian alone on the pedastal.

Two stats in particular stand out. The first: with his fifth goal in his ninth league appearance at 20 years and 17 days, he became the second-youngest Rossoneri player to reach this milestone in his first 10 appearances in the three-points-for-a-win era, after Pato (18 years and 181 days).

Second: he is one of only three players born in 2006 or later in the five major European leagues in 2026-27 to have scored at least eight goals in all competitions, along with Yamal (13) and Brunner (8).

Oh, and there’s another pretty good one: Shevchenko also scored eight goals in his first 13 games of the season with the Diavolo (although he achieved this in fewer minutes). The reward could well be a renewal, to fend off Premier League interest too.

#1536. Brazilian Alysson becomes a starter after injury-hit first year at Villa

By Alexis Pereira | 10 Nov 2026 18:30

Alysson has taken advantage of Aston Villa’s rebuild to establish himself in unai Emery’s side, scoring in last Sunday’s 4-4 draw with Manchester United. The Brazilian winger, who joined from Gremio in January, has overcome an injury-hit first six months to become a starter in the Premier League.

Aston Villa’s season has been defined by resilience. The team lost more than half of its starters in the last transfer window, but Emery, with many signings, has reinvented his group again. They went seven games unbeaten before the current run of four without a win. Part of that change has come from a Brazilian who was already there: Alysson.

Signed in January from Gremio at the age of 19, he suffered in the first half of the year. Three different injuries kept him out of 18 games, according to Transfermarkt. As a result, he only played three games for Villa, coming off the bench against Brighton and Hove Albion and Wolverhampton Wanderers (both in February) and Chelsea (March).

‘He spent more time injured than available to train and play,’ Emery admitted last month about the player’s previous season.

With a full pre-season, the Brazilian was able to change his status and string games together. On Sunday, he scored one of the goals in the 4-4 draw with United, in a standout performance. It is an unlikely story given the right winger’s age and the pressure of the Premier League, where Gustavo Nunes, a former Gremio team-mate of Alysson, has still not made a start for Brentford, the club he has played for since August 2024.

More reliable physically, thanks to a full pre-season, the youngster was able to be available more often and take advantage of the overhaul in Villa’s attack following the departures of Morgan Rogers, Ollie Watkins and Leon Bailey. In his first months he was compared to the Jamaican winger.

‘He has more or less similar characteristics or qualities to Bailey: he is left-footed and plays on the right,’ Emery said in February. ‘And he has huge potential.’

In the first game of 2026-27, he showed he would have more time on the pitch, playing 17 minutes in the defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Super Cup. He then came off the bench in the next eight games, with a short break for a muscle problem in September, and his performances earned him a starting place.

Introduced at half-time in the defeat to Nottingham Forest, he arrived in the box to head in and level the score. Against Fenerbahce, he produced a good individual move on the wing, went past a defender into the area and passed for Tammy Abraham to tap in. Those displays earned him starts against Newcastle United, Viking, Manchester City, Fulham and, finally, Manchester United. Against Viking, he had a standout match for his ability to dribble and win duels, and directly caused an own goal.

At Old Trafford, he did everything but make it rain. He opened the scoring with a first-time shot through goalkeeper Senne Lammens’ legs, forced the Belgian’s rebound for Nicolas Jackson’s goal, and won the penalty converted by McGinn when he went at Diogo Dalot and was brought down. He could also have scored again, but a chip over Lammens went wide.

‘Alysson is understanding things well and is giving us what I want,’ Emery said in September.

‘Every minute he is playing, practising, he is fantastic,’ Emery added in October. ‘We can see his power. We can see that if he can get consistency, a lot of things he is doing: “Wow!”’

The numbers illustrate his role. Villa have been much more vertical this season thanks to the speed of Jackson, Johan Manzambi, George Hemmings and, of course, Alysson. The Brazilian ranks second of all players in the Premier League for sprints, with 22.7, and reached 35.4km/h in one match, the highest by a Villa player and the eighth-highest in the league, according to Sofascore. In the Champions League, despite only one start and 127 minutes across four games, he is among the leaders for successful dribbles (nine, 11th in the competition level with Jackson) and ground duels won (16).

‘Alysson was incredible,’ said Villa midfielder Emiliano Buendia after the 3-1 win over Viking. ‘He is showing all his potential and his ability to play on the wings.’

Because of his age, being in his first year in a new country and the injury history, Emery is cautious with the Brazilian. In different interviews, the Spanish manager has praised the youngster while stressing he still has a lot to learn, especially tactically.

‘He should be a player who can help us. So we need to be patient, seek consistency and be careful with him every day,’ he said on 19 October. ‘This season, he has felt some pain and we need to try to be careful, but also give him confidence so he is comfortable.’

‘Alysson is improving his consistency because he has very good individual qualities, but he also needs to understand the importance of consistency in the collective aspect: defending, attacking, positioning and understanding combinations with team-mates,’ he explained two days later.

Emery remains an admirer and sees the right winger as a possible Brazil international. ‘My expectation is that Alysson can also get there,’ he said after the call-up of Villa team-mate Joao Gomes. At 20, the forward has shown on the pitch what he can do, and if he becomes more consistent, it is only a matter of time before he is called up.

A first Serie A goal from a Bosnian teenager and a late curler from a substitute gave Juventus victory over Napoli on Sunday 1 November 2026. The game at the Allianz Stadium was goalless at half-time. It finished 2-0.

#1534. Kevin De Bruyne: Premier League club ‘assessing real chances’ of signing Man City legend from Napoli

By Oliver Thomas | 10 Nov 2026 18:58, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 19:01

One Premier League club are reportedly considering a shock move for Napoli and Belgium playmaker Kevin De Bruyne in January.

The 35-year-old spent 10 glorious years at Manchester City and earned legendary status at the Etihad Stadium where he won 19 trophies and made 422 appearances, scoring 108 goals and registering 177 assists.

City decided not to extend De Bruyne’s contract at the end of the 2024-25 season and he subsequently signed for Napoli as a free agent, embarking on a fresh challenge in Italian football.

De Bruyne’s debut campaign with Napoli was stuck by injury and he was limited to only 16 starts across all competitions, but he has since played in all 15 games across Serie A and the Champions League this term, chipping in with four goals and two assists.

The playmaker’s current contract is due to expire in June 2027, but it has been suggested that he could leave Napoli sooner than expected.

Last month, former Napoli striker Roberto Carlos Sosa stated that the “spark never really ignited” between De Bruyne and the Naples outfit.

Italian news outlet Calciomercato have since reported that De Bruyne is going through a ‘mental decline’ and the midfielder make look to pursue a sensational return to the Premier League in January.

The report adds that Everton would be interested in signing De Bruyne and have already initiated ‘first contacts’ with the player’s representatives to understand their ‘real chances’ of signing him.

In order for the transfer to materialise, Napoli would need to be convinced to sanction De Bruyne’s exit midway through the season, and it remains unknown as to whether they would demand a fee for a player with six months remaining on his contract.

De Bruyne is widely regarded as one of the best midfielders in Premier League history and thrived as an advanced playmaker at Man City behind the central striker.

He was also capable of operating as a false nine or in a deep-lying midfield role, dictating play from just in front of the back four, while he also has experience out on the right and left flanks, though he does not possess the acceleration he once had.

At Everton, De Bruyne could be a contender to play in a deeper midfield position alongside James Garner and/or Harrison Armstrong, who have featured regularly under David Moyes.

De Bruyne could also play further forward as a No.10, but this is where Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall has established himself as a key first-team figure with the Toffees.

Alternatively, the Belgian could rivals Brennan Johnson, Tyler Dibling and Merlin Rohl for starts on the right side of midfield.

Regardless of which position De Bruyne would play under Moyes, the midfielder would want assurances of regular first-team football before agreeing to join Everton or any other club should he leave Napoli.

Juventus will travel to AZ Alkmaar without Weston McKennie. The American has fatigue in his adductor and will sit out Thursday’s Europa League match. The news is not all bad. Kerim Alajbegović and Juan Cabal, who also came off in the 2-0 win over Napoli, have both been cleared.

McKennie lasted only the first half at the Allianz Stadium. Federico Gatti replaced him at the break. Luciano Spalletti had to send on an extra defender because McKennie felt a pull in his adductor. The coach also had few other players to choose from.

Alajbegović had both a goal and a scare against Napoli. He opened the scoring in the 70th minute and was replaced by Jérémie Boga two minutes later. Boga then added the second in the 87th. Published: 04:00 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 08:16 EST, 8 November 2026

Manchester United legends reunited to raise a glass to Sir Alex Ferguson on his anniversary of being named manager of the club on Saturday night.

In a decision that ushered in the most successful period in United's history, Ferguson was poached from Scottish club Aberdeen 40 years ago on Friday – with the iconic manager lifting 37 pieces of silverware during his spell at Old Trafford.

He also played a significant role in shaping the careers of a litany of stars who graced the club during his 27-year tenure, with the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo, Wayne Rooney and David Beckham hugely benefiting from his mentorship.

And a handful of players who shared a dressing room with Ferguson were on hand to toast the iconic manager during a celebratory evening in Manchester on Saturday night.

Diehard United fan and actor James Nesbitt shared a group photo on Instagram, featuring Ferguson alongside current United boss Michael Carrick.

Nemanja Vidic, Robin van Persie, Darren Fletcher, Jonny Evans, Javier Hernandez and John O'Shea also joined their old mentor at the bash.

Actor and Man United fan James Nesbitt posted this picture with club royalty - clockwise from front left: Jonny Evans, Darren Fletcher, Robin van Persie, Nemanja Vidic, Michael Carrick, John O'Shea, Sir Alex Ferguson, Edwin van der Sar and Javier Hernandez

Ferguson ushered in the most successful period in the club's history during his 27-year stint

Carrick has namechecked Ferguson as a crucial ally as he looks to transform United's fortunes amid the club's worst ever start to a Premier League season.

The Red Devils dropped into the relegation zone on Saturday night following Nottingham Forest's win over Manchester City, and Carrick's stint in the dugout appeared all but over following a 3-0 thumping by Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

But he was handed a reprieve by the United hierarchy and there were green shoots of optimism following a rousing 3-2 comeback victory over Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

United host Unai Emery's Aston Villa at Old Trafford today, and Carrick has admitted he has been given no guarantees on his future.

'Whatever is going to happen is going to happen. I'm really looking forward to the next game, playing at home on the back of the other night,' he said.

'The supporters are hopefully looking forward to coming energised and feeling good about what they might see, and we've got to repay that.'

Carrick is preparing for a normal international break, and doesn't have any plans to spend more time with his family after a turbulent period at Old Trafford.

'Not really different to normal. Genuinely not,' he added. 'I think international breaks are always a time to re-energise and freshen up. Some of the players that go away to internationals get freshened up in a different environment, but I don't really need it. I'm fine as I am.

'We'll certainly train next week and maybe have the weekend off. We'll see how that develops, who's left behind, who's with us and what they need.'

What a fantastic evening at Old Trafford celebrating 40 years of Sir Alex taking the reign at @ManUtd. Catching up with the boys and some great speeches about how he achieved to leave such a mark on this club! pic.twitter.com/kgoNfzfPWJ

Ferguson unveiled as new manager of Manchester United in 1986

Carrick insisted that he and Bruno Fernandes have put any issues behind them after the United captain criticised his tactics in the Champions League defeat to Como last month.

After he led United's fightback against Roma in midweek by converting a twice taken penalty, Fernandes confirmed that Carrick's decision to drop him for the Bournemouth game was due to a loss of form, and disputed that the two men had a clear-the-air meeting over his comments.

But Carrick said: 'There are always conversations, bits going on; acknowledging certain things of when things are going well, what we need to improve on as a group.

'Sometimes it's individually, sometimes it's group. We always have discussions. What's actually said in that discussion, I'll keep that to myself.

'But I think it's pretty clear we've moved in a good direction, and Bruno's commitment is undoubted for me (in terms) of what he brings to this team and this club.

'He showed that again this week by his actions, the way he's played and how he dealt with even retaking the penalty and the frame of mind he was in for that. I think that tells you everything. Bruno's as good as ever.'

#1530. Man United news: INEOS and Jim Ratcliffe make Omar Berrada, Jason Wilcox 'sack' call as Michael Carrick edges towards exit

By Lewis Nolan | 10 Nov 2026 19:11

Manchester co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe still has confidence in director of football Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada, the latest report has claimed.

The future of several figures at Old Trafford have been questioned in recent weeks given the club find themselves 18th in the Premier League table.

Head coach Michael Carrick appears likely to lose his job after Wednesday, when senior leaders of Ratcliffe's INEOS group are set to meet to discuss the manager's future.

Wilcox and Berrada will reportedly be in attendance, though fans have been critical of their role in the downfall of the Red Devils and have called for their dismissal.

The Telegraph claim that both retain the support of INEOS and Ratcliffe, who has no plans to remove them from their roles.

Berrada and Wilcox were appointed in 2024, with the former having previously worked for Manchester City in a number of departments, including recruitment strategy.

Wilcox took up a role as Southampton's director of football in January 2023, and he was reportedly identified by Berrada as a key talent.

It is impossible for fans to know the true extent of their roles at Old Trafford, but the fact that United have repeatedly failed in the transfer market is a damning indictment of their time at the club.

The Red Devils focused on their attack in the summer of 2025, only for the likes of Matheus Cunha and Benjamin Sesko to disappoint, and there is still no clear left-winger in the squad other than Marcus Rashford.

United signed three midfielders in the summer of 2026, but there are serious question marks about Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, while Carlos Baleba has struggled with injuries.

Carrick will almost certainly be relived of his coaching duties, and while results and performances suggest that it would be the right call, he has been routinely let down by those above him.

A squad's ceiling will ultimately be capped by how well the decision makers recruit in transfer markets, and the likes of Berrada and Wilcox have left the manager short in numerous areas.

Responsibility for United's struggles must ultimately fall on Ratcliffe, especially as Carrick is set to be the third boss sacked since he took control of sporting operations in 2024.

#1528. Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players

Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso said: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

“Yeah, it’s all maybe entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win and we don’t give these entertaining moments,” he said.

“But, for sure, it kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to... or it will take moments to fix them when we get the lead and you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially in the first goal, we can do much better.

“It was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances. But that momentum that we had changed the mood and the score of the game, and it’s something that we need to be talking [about], we address and we will get better. But it’s having an impact on our performances at the moment.”

Asked if his players have a real desire to defend and keep clean sheets, Alonso said: “We can do better, we can do better for sure. We need to know that even when we have the lead, a very important part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distance, to go intense in the situations to defend. I’m sure that we can do better.

“Overall, I think that we are attacking better than defending in every part. We know that it’s a big topic and a big theme for us. For sure, it’s just four games. But the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it and we need to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”

Needing three goals or more to win games is not sustainable, as Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is finding out.

This is not a problem of Alonso’s making, given Chelsea have now gone 20 Premier League games without a clean sheet. But he is certainly not improving the issue yet.

Chelsea beat Fulham with three goals and Brighton with four but left themselves far too much to do against Arsenal and were taken advantage of by Hull City, who will be slightly disappointed they did not leave Stamford Bridge with all three points.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez has now conceded seven goals in three games since joining from Aston Villa, while central defender Maxence Lacroix, who joined for £52m from Crystal Palace in the summer, was relegated to the substitutes’ bench.

Martínez was at fault for Mohamed Belloumi’s second goal, but the Argentine did make a crucial save at his back post to stop substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho grabbing a winner that Chelsea could have had no complaints about.

Hull finished the game with more shots on goal than their hosts and a higher expected-goals rate. Chelsea are far too open and in some ways far too entertaining.

Defensive midfielder Moisés Caicedo cannot return from injury quickly enough, but this does not feel like a problem that will be solved by one man. Alonso needs to find a balance and instil a real desire in his team to defend.

Caicedo has that desire, but there are no defenders at the club who have shown that absolute desperation to keep the ball out of the net that Chelsea fans became so used to in the days of John Terry, Gary Cahill and César Azpilicueta.

None of this should diminish Hull’s performance. They were not only spirited and full of character but also showed quality and a threat. The joke is currently on those who laughed at their hopes of survival before a ball had been kicked.

It is now two wins and two draws for Sergej Jakirovic’s team and they are already a fifth of the way to 40 points. Jakirovic had promised his staff a week off in the international break if they reached eight points after five games. With that target already met, there may be a new reward if Hull can make it 11 points against Newcastle United next weekend.

“Before the season, I said to my staff that we will take seven, eight points in these first five and then I will give them seven days off,” Jakirovic said. “That was our target and now we are in a very good position, eight points.

“Especially today, it’s very, very difficult to play here, and now we will try to get even more. Of course, I’m a little bit worried about the international break because we have 13 national team players. But we will see who will come back and in what condition. So this is my concern right now.” Asked if his staff’s seven-day break will be extended if Hull can beat Newcastle, Jakirovic added: “I will tell them. But I know already.”

While his five-game target may need modifying, Jakirovic is not deviating from his goal for the season for Hull. “Our target is always to stay in the league and collect as many points as possible,” he said. “Forty points, 38 to 41, this is the average we need. Then it’s easier to play. You can play more relaxed, with more joy and happiness. So [get to] this as soon as possible, so that we are safe.”

Hull had not conceded a league goal before this and there had been predictions they might crumble when they finally let the ball into their net. They did so after just seven minutes but they kept their heads and came back stronger.

It was far too easy for Morgan Rogers to make a yard of space for himself to shoot after collecting the ball from João Pedro, and Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis may not have been happy to have been beaten at his near post.

Chelsea have now scored inside the first 10 minutes in all of their four league games, but Hull were in no mood to crumble and hit back with two goals in six minutes from Belloumi to take a half-time lead. Both Hull goals were shockers from Chelsea’s perspective. The first, in the 28th minute, came as a result of Jorrel Hato letting the ball bounce over him from a Ryan Giles cross and Belloumi finished brilliantly.

Belloumi’s second came after Martínez had flapped at a corner and Semi Ajayi had hit the bar with a header. The ball fell to Belloumi again and his shot was deflected into the net.

It was no surprise that Hato did not reappear for the second half, as he was replaced by Pep Chavarría at left-back. But Chelsea remained vulnerable and Martínez had to recover from spilling a Regan Slater shot to prevent Ollie McBurnie extending Hull’s advantage.

When Palmer and Pedro combined for Pedro to sweep the ball into the net and equalise with 24 minutes remaining, it seemed like it would be Chelsea who would provide the grandstand finish.

But it was Hull who got a second wind and Chelsea were indebted to Martínez for making a save to stop Cho securing all three points and sending the visiting fans home even happier.

I feel good. We have to be happy. It’s a huge result for us.

We had 2-1 at half-time and we had a 100 per cent chance with McBurnie but Martinez’s save was excellent. We have to control play better in the box because we can stop this [Chelsea goal]. We had an excellent chance for Cho – Martinez saved again. Player of the match.

We can be very happy. We took a point in a very demanding match.

Eight points against very difficult opponents. We have to continue like this.

There have been 12 Premier League games at Anfield in 2026, Liverpool have only won 4 of them to date. This was seventh draw and Fulham deserves their share of the spoils. This was very much a learning experience for Andoni Iraola.

Not a single home win in the Premier League, today.

Aston Villa 1 Nottingham Forest 2Bournemouth 2 Brentford 2Chelsea 2 Hull City 2Crystal Palace 2 Ipswich Town 3Liverpool 0 Fulham 0

What a result for Hull, who remain unbeaten and they have taken five points from fixtures against United, Villa and Chelsea.

That is the first really poor result of the Alonso era, points dropped.

What a thriller in SE25, both teams have been going for it in the closing stages, but Ipswich have surely score the winner through Zian Flemming.

Fulham were pointless before this game, but they have kept a clean sheet at Anfield with a disciplined display and they could well have score one or two. Underwhelming for Liverpool, who have not won just one of their first four games and their fixtures have not been the most taxing.

And as we predicted at the beginning of the game... Liverpool 0 Fulham 0. If this reporter ever gives you advice on a horse to back or a team to follow, make sure you take the opposite stance. Fulham deserve their reward and their fans are singing “We got a point!”

Villa are finishing the game with 10 men because Ian Maatsen pulled up after Emery had made his five substitutions, and Forest have punished them through Igor Jesus with just a few minutes of normal time to play.

Alexander Isak heads over the bar when he perhaps should have hit the target. Has time run out for Liverpool?

You might imagine Chelsea are battering down the door, but Mohamed-Ali Cho has just forced Emi Martinez into a save at the other end. Hull will remain unbeaten if they can hold out.

Strand Larsen has had his critics, but he has scored his first goal of the season to set up a grandstand finish with 15 minutes plus stoppage time to play at Selhurst Park.

Short corner, McGinn whipped in an inswinging cross that is glanced into the bottom corner by Alysson.

Liverpool continue to toil at Anfield, but no opening goal. Iraola has thrown on Frimpong, Mac Allister, Ngumoha and Gakpo in the second half. Fulham have had the chances to score at least one, and Josh King has just brought a save out of Alisson.

Hull are a little lucky they still have 11 men on the pitch. Already on a booking, my man Crooks bundled down Rogers. It could easily have been another yellow car but the referee let him off and now he’s been replaced by Iroegbunam.

Joao Pedro finds the smallest of gaps to be the goalkeeper and find the roof of the net with a brilliant, instinctive finish.

That had not really been coming for Chelsea. It all felt a bit easy for Palmer to get his low cross into the box and Pedro to sweep the ball in. The home fans have woken up again.

Martinez was lucky to get away with another slip up, there. He spilt Slater’s shot but reacted before McBurnie to stop the Hull striker scoring the rebound. Just a day after his nasty looking crash, Sorba Thomas is on for Hull.

This game is absolutely here for Fulham to win. Quietness has descended around Anfield, the hosts have no fluency in their play and Fulham are growing in confidence. Why wouldn’t they after getting to 65 minutes with a clean sheet?

Just like in the first half, four minutes after one of these teams taking the lead there has been an equaliser. Kevin Scahde is in a rich vein of form.

Bournemouth have have never beaten Brentford in the Premier League, but they might well be on their way to changing that record having trailed earlier in the game. Marcus Tavernier has just scored their second goal.

Matt Davidson Rider Crooks has just been booked for a very cynical foul on Rogers. It gave Chelsea a free-kick in a dangerous position Reece James had an effort tipped away. Chelsea have started the second half well

Within a minute of the restart, Villa lose the ball in midfield and Delap punishes them to the maximum. Cracking finish from just outside the box, and a much-needed goal by Delap. The Glasner curse striking for Emery again?

Liam Delap has just started paying back that £50m transfer fee with a fine goal.

Delap picked the ball up on the left and set himself up on the edge of the box before crashing a 25-yard shot past Zion Suzuki.

Unai Emery has made a couple of changes at half-time, taking off Nicolas Jackson who picked up a silly booking just before half-time.

Tammy Abraham is on in his place. George Hemmings is also off and replaced by Alysson.

Pep Chavarria on for Chelsea at half-time. He’s replaced Jorrel Hato, who had a bit of a stinker in the first half.

Andoni Iraola hasn’t hung about here. Milos Kerkez has come on immediately after half-time for Kostas Tsimikas and you can say with certainty that Liverpool will be shopping for a new left-back in due course.

So at half-time, Hull City are top of the Premier League and don’t their supporters know it? They were singing “we are top of the League” for the full two minutes of time added on for stoppages at the end of the first period. Alonso has some work to do at the break.

Forest did need a brilliant double save from Matz Sels to deny Victor Lindelof and have recovered to slow the match down.

Neco Williams wasted a decent chance for Forest from outside the penalty area shortly before the break.

Referee Andrew Madley has irritated both teams with a number of weird decisions - but that’s sadly par for the course with officials nowadays.

Villa 0 Forest 0Bournemouth 1 Brentford 1Chelsea 1 Hull City 2Palace 1 Ipswich 2Liverpool 0 Fulham 0

Palace in some trouble now, level with Ipswich and down to 10 men. Disasi was sent off in the 34th minute for a reckless challenge on Jack Clarke, caught him with studs on shin.

Things got worse for Palace just before half-time, with Leif Davis heading home at the back post to give Ipswich the league.

Apologies for the lack of updates, some technical gremlins at Telegraph Towers. A nip and tuck game as expected at at the Vitality: Kevin Schade gave Brentford the lead before Justin Kluivert equalised four minutes later.

One way to put it is that Kostas Tsimikas isn’t playing well. Another way to say it would be that his efforts are making Milos Kerkez look like Roberto Carlos. The Greek left-back is having a dreadful afternoon and Fulham are getting plenty of joy out of him. We suggested there was no chance of this game finishing goalless, and it’s anomalous that we have reached 40 minutes without score. Fulham, certainly, have a sense of adventure and have been into Liverpool’s 18-yard box plenty of times. Let’s see if the picture changes before the interval.

That’s now seven goals Emi Martinez has conceded in three games since joining from Villa to supposedly solve Chelsea’s goalkeeping crisis. Martinez won’t be pleased with Hull’s second goal, here. He was beaten to a corner by Ajayi. His header hit the bar and Belloumi’s shot was deflected past him. The Hull fans are in dreamland.

This is a turn up for the books. Chelsea undone by a long ball forward, and Hato lets the ball bounce over his head, and Belloumi finishes with aplomb.

That’s now 20 Premier League games Chelsea have gone without keeping a clean sheet. What an earth was Jorrel Hato doing, letting the ball bounce over him for Belloumi? Amateur stuff at the back from the home side. It was Hull’s first meaningful attack.

Emersonn has struggled in some games so far this season, but he has just planted a header into the corner from a Davis cross.

There is a VAR check for offside... but the goal stands.

5 - Morgan Rogers is the fifth different player to score or assist in each of Chelsea's first four games of a Premier League season, after Didier Drogba (2010-11), Cesc Fàbregas (2014-15), Diego Costa (2014-15 & 2016-17), and Eden Hazard (2018-19).Famous. pic.twitter.com/0cuThzH472

A sweet strike from one of Palace’s summer signings, recruited from Union Saint Gilloise, and that is his first Palace goal. The 22-year-old Israeli came through at Maccabi Haifa. Uphill task for Gary O’Neill and Ipswich.

Austin MacPhee, Chelsea’s flamboyant set-piece coach, just motioned for Xabi Alonso to sit down when the Blues manager momentarily got up from his seat when the home side were preparing to take a corner. It seems MacPhee wears the (correct length) trousers when it comes to set pieces.

An almighty let off for Alisson and Liverpool after pass from the goalkeeper played Gravenberch into trouble, but Jacquet cleared off the line to keep the game goalless. That was Fulham’s first foray forward.

A bright start in this game and there is no chance it will end goalless (famous last words). Andoni Iraola has made three changes from the team that beat Atletico Madrid on Wednesday and it’s a pattern of his early management that he is making the kind of decisions that supporters are nodding along in approval with. Liverpool should already be one up but Alexander Isak’s shot has just drifted across the face of goal but the signs are encouraging. It could be a long afternoon for Alvaro Arbeloa.

Wow. Unbelievable double save from Forest’s Matz Sels there to keep out Victor Lindelof.

The first was the most impressive, a reflex stop after a deflection.

Morgan Rogers is the first player to score against Hull City this season. Emi Martinez launched the ball forward after claiming a corner, and Rogers’ shot from the edge of the area crept under the goalkeeper Tzolakis. He will not want to watch that one again.

We’re past five minutes and it’s the longest Chelsea have gone without scoring in the league this season. Back on Matt Crooks – one of his middle names is Rider.

Although Rogers scored in the seventh minute...so the early goals continue for Chelsea. It will be difficult for Hull now.

Twelve seconds in and the chant “where were you in Istanbul” gets a very early airing from Villa’s home fans.

That is of course a reference to Villa’s 4-0 win over Forest in the Europa League semi-final second leg last season.

The early indications are that Reece James is playing in midfield with Malo Gusto at right-back in a conventional back four.

Xabi Alonso has made an encouraging start to life as Chelsea manager. But his trousers upset me. They are three inches too short and a bit baggy above the ankle.

We are under way in the five Premier League 3pm kick-offs. Goals and further updates from around the grounds as they happen.

Some early #analysis from Matt at the Bridge, about one of Hull’s midfielders.

One player who has really shone for Villa so far this season is teenage midfielder George Hemmings.

Unai Emery has been very impressed with the academy graduate, who made his Champions League debut on Tuesday night.

There is also a big buzz around £51m signing Johan Manzambi, who is on the bench today after recovering from a knee injury.

Will we get another fast start from Chelsea today? They have scored inside the first five minutes in all three of their League games this season. Hull are yet to concede.

Dominic King writes that there were signs of promise in the relationship between Barcola, Wirtz and Isak in Liverpool’s win over Atletico Madrid, and all three forwards start against Fulham. Timothy Castagne, Fulham’s right-back will need to have his sprinting boots on against Barcola, who is grease lightning.

Cole Palmer has 15 goal involvements in his 15 Premier League games for Chelsea against newly promoted sides.9 goals ⚽6 assists 🅰️ pic.twitter.com/PJIU0YxIhQ

I’m having real fun. I’ve got a smile on face and I’m enjoying my football. Playing with players like [Palmer and Joao Pedro] inspire you to be better and make you do better and do well for the team. We are in a good moment and we want to keep it going.

Hull are really tough to beat. They have played against some good opponents and they’ve kept them out - they haven’t conceded yet. It is going to be difficult because they are really organised but we are at home and it is on us to make the game about us.

We know it is always tough against Brentford. We can expect a tight game today, definitely. We both want to win so it’ll be a nice game.

We are very excited about our first European game coming up but we haven’t really spoken about it lately because we have just spoken about this game. This is a big game and we are looking for our first three points of the season. We have been close in every game so we hope to get it today.

Unai Emery is possibly the best coach in the Premier League but has found past encounters with Oliver Glasner very uncomfortable.

Since Glasner’s arrival in English football with Crystal Palace in February 2024, he has faced Emery’s Villa seven times and never lost.

With five victories and two draws, it is an impressive record albeit with a different set of players.

Aston Villa and Forest are two teams in transition, and meet for the first time since that two-legged Europa League semi-final last season.

Villa are building a new chapter after a summer of significant change, while Forest are implementing a totally different style of play under Oliver Glasner.

There have been signs of progress at both of the former European Cup winners. Villa secured an impressive victory over Club Brugge in the Champions League on Tuesday. Forest are improving under Glasner, with their best performance the 2-2 draw at Liverpool.

Returning to Villa Park will have some bitter memories for a number of the Forest players, after that 4-0 defeat in the second leg of the Europa League.

Ollie Watkins and Emi Martinez departed for pastures new in the transfer window.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this afternoon’s Premier League three o’clock kick-offs, and home bankers would appear to be the theme of the day.

Liverpool will be strongly fancied to put Fulham to the sword at Anfield, with confidence low at the London club and new manager Alvaro Arbeloa (once a player at Anfield) already under pressure amid reports of dressing room unrest. Andoni Iraola secured his first Premier League victory as Liverpool manager at Ipswich last time out, and backed up that result with a come-from-behind win against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

Chelsea host Hull City, who are unbeaten after three games and have yet to concede a goal. It is a remarkable start to the season for Sergej Jakirović‘s side, who continue to defy expectations as well as the underlying data. For all their spirit and defensive organisation, keeping out Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro at Stamford Bridge promises to be a tall order, though.

Aston Villa’s rocky start to the campaign took a turn for the better with a 3-2 Champions League victory at Club Brugge, and as the weeks go by Unai Emery’s team should grow stronger as their raft of young signings bed in. Nottingham Forest could be obdurate opponents, although Villa swept them aside in the second leg of last season’s Europa League semi-final. Oliver Glasner’s Crystal Palace were a bogey team for Villa though, with the Austrian coach undefeated against Emery having notched up some resounding victories.

Glasner’s former club Palace could do with a home win against Ipswich Town, while there is cigarette paper between Bournemouth and Brentford, two of the league’s smartest operators who play at the Vitality Stadium this afternoon. Bournemouth qualified for Europe at Brentford’s expense last season, but Marco Rose is looking for his first league win despite some encouraging performances.

#1527. TMW: Milan temptation behind Palladino’s chaotic summer – the reconstruction

A report has revealed some of the background on Raffaele Palladino’s turbulent summer, mentioning AC Milan among other clubs.

TMW have provided a reconstruction of what has been a turbulent past few months for Palladino. Since he took over at Bologna, they have won five of seven games in the league – including at San Siro against Milan – to climb up to eighth in the league.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In the summer, Palladino turned down a long-term contract with Atalanta because he was linked with more prestigious jobs, but this left him without a job. Then, when Bologna parted ways with Domenico Tedesco, the Italian took his talents to Reggio Emilia and has not looked back.

Why didn’t he stay in Bergamo? The question arises naturally, considering the results obtained and qualification for the Conference despite a stuttering start. Palladino – after the victory against Borussia Dortmund – was considered the future for La Dea.

There was a contract ready to continue together until 2029, but everything seemed to turn sour. The three-year contract that was then offered to Maurizio Sarri, because Atalanta needed a decision quickly and Palladino wanted time to reflect.

His contract with Atalanta expired in 2027, and he wasn’t in a hurry to sign another. The second thoughts didn’t sit well with Atalanta but Palladino later backtracked, offering to accept the previous contract, even offering to shorten it to 2028.

Meanwhile, Atalanta’s league performance worsened and they failed to reach the Coppa Italia final, against Sarri himself. Relations, now strained, finally broke down.

The truth is that the former Monza coach was waiting to see which vacancies came up. Napoli in particular were a club he was monitoring closely, when Antonio Conte announced his departure. Palladino, along with Vincenzo Italiano, was a strong name.

There could also have been an opportunity at Milan when Massimiliano Allegri departed. However, as is known, the Rossoneri decided to pursue Andoni Iraola and then turned to Ruben Amorim, clearly not inclined to bet on a coach who knows the league. Palladino would have been keen, it seems.

#1526. Exor pays in €60m of Juventus’ €250m raise, but UEFA deal limits January plans

Juventus shareholders have cleared a capital increase of up to €250m, and majority owner Exor has already committed €60m of it. Giovanni Carnevali warned that the UEFA settlement means nothing extraordinary should be expected in January.

Juventus shareholders gave the board the power to raise up to €250m in new capital at the Allianz Stadium on 3 November. The vote came in the extraordinary part of the meeting and passed with 99.9% in favour. The same assembly approved the 2025/26 accounts.

Part of the money is already committed. Exor has already paid in €60m as an advance towards the capital increase. That payment supports the club’s equity and finances until the board uses its new authority. The majority owner has also guaranteed its own 65.4% stake in the raise and any shares other investors leave untaken.

The squad will not see the full sum. Shoring up the club’s finances across this season and next will take 45–50% of whatever is raised, according to Football Italia. That leaves roughly €100m mainly for first-team signings before the January window. Beyond keeping equity at a suitable level, the rest will go on controlling debt and keeping the team competitive, including transfers, Corriere dello Sport reports.

The accounts show why the balance sheet needs support. The consolidated loss for 2025/26 was €66.0m. That was €7.9m bigger than the previous year’s €58.1m. The result was in line with the forecasts in the club’s half-year report to 31 December 2025. The board had approved the accounts on 29 September. Another loss is expected in 2026/27, mainly because Juventus are in the Europa League rather than the Champions League.

The assembly was Giovanni Carnevali’s first as chief executive. He promised a serious approach to the January window. His warning was just as clear. As a serious company, Juventus must honour its settlement agreement with UEFA and does not expect to do anything extraordinary.

That agreement was announced on 30 June. It is a three-year settlement with the First Chamber of UEFA’s Club Financial Control Body. It relates to Juventus breaking UEFA’s Football Earnings Rule over the three seasons from 2022/23 to 2024/25.

For supporters, the message is mixed. The capital increase gives the club fresh resources. The settlement still dictates how quickly that money can be used on the pitch.

Shareholders also criticised the club for keeping a low profile in recent years. President Gianluca Ferrero declared Juventus open to dialogue with Tether.

The terms of the UEFA deal leave little margin. Missing the targets agreed with UEFA for the current season or the next two can lead to limits on the club’s UEFA List A and further sporting sanctions. The settlement runs until the 2027/28 financial year.

#1525. Ghana vs Somalia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Ojele | 10 Nov 2026 20:14, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 20:24

Ghana will be desperate to breathe life into their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign when they play host to Somalia at the Essipong Sports Stadium in the first of their Group C double-header on Thursday.

Having lost their first two matches, both nations are left with little room for mistakes and know Thursday’s result could prove decisive in shaping up their qualifying ambitions, and this makes for an exciting contest in Sekondi-Takoradi.

Two games into the race for a spot in the 2027 AFCON, Ghana find themselves amongst nine sides yet to pick up any points in the qualifiers, with the federation parting ways with Portuguese coach Carlos Queiroz and opting for a change in ideas in the dugout.

Coming off the back of a round-of-32 defeat against Colombia in the World Cup back in June, the Black Stars kicked off their AFCON qualifying campaign with a 2-0 loss against Ivory Coast on September 24, with Malick Yalcouye and Franck Kessie netting on either side of half-time to hand the Elephants all three points.

Playing in front of the home supporters five days later, Ghana failed to make home advantage count in matchday two, when they fell to a 4-2 defeat at the hands of Gambia after squandering a two-goal lead at the Accra Sports Stadium.

Ernest Nuamah and Felix Afena-Gyan hit the target to put Ghana in the driver’s seat, but strikes from Muhammed Badamosi, Omar Colley, and a second-half brace from Konyaspor striker Ebrima Colley turned the game on its head for Gambia.

The four-time African champions have now gone eight straight games without a win in the Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, a run which saw them miss out on the 2025 AFCON, failing to feature in the continental showpiece for the first time since 2004.

Now tasked with restoring confidence and flipping the script, interim coach Kim Lars Bjorkegren faces a must-win assignment on Thursday as Ghana seek to avoid missing back-to-back AFCON tournaments for the first time since their three successive absences in 1986, 1988 and 1990.

Like the home side, Somalia journey to the Essipong Sports Stadium with the same urgent need for a result if they are to turn their fortunes around and secure a first-ever qualification for the Africa Cup of Nations.

Having edged out Eswatini and Mauritius in the preliminary phase, the Ocean Stars fell to a 2-1 loss against Gambia in the Group C opener on September 25, with Ebrima Colley and Muhammed Badamosi netting on either side of Bilal Njie’s 72nd-minute equaliser to hand the hosts all three points at the Independence Stadium.

While there were positives to take from the defeat against Gambia, Somalia were left spitting feathers four days later, when they fell to a 2-0 defeat against Ivory Coast through strikes from Yann Gboho and Bazoumana Toure in the final six minutes at the Stade Felix Houphouet-Boigny.

Yusuf Ali’s men demonstrated their ability to rise to the occasion against quality opposition last time out when they pushed Ivory Coast to the limit, and they will have reason to believe they can upset the odds against a Ghana side currently far from convincing.

Ghana Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Somalia Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Newly-appointed Ghana boss Bjorkegren has called up 26 players to the squad for October’s double-header with Somalia, including the Premier League trio of Abdul Fatawu Issahaku, Brandon Thomas-Asante and Ibrahim Osman.

Having missed the first two qualifying matches through a groin problem, Jordan Ayew has been recalled to the squad, and the nation’s captain will hope his leadership and wealth of experience can count for something.

The Black Stars will also be lifted by the return of Tottenham Hotspur forward Mohammed Kudus, who is set to make his first international appearance of the year after missing the World Cup through an injury.

Manchester City forward Antoine Semenyo misses out through a knee injury, while 31-year-old defender Jan Gyamerah, who made his debut against Mexico on May 26, is also ruled out through a muscle problem.

Before their late collapse, Somalia held their own against a superior and more experienced Ivory Coast side last time out, and we expect Ali to name a similar XI on Thursday, with Mohamed Mohamed, Abel Gigli, Ali Omar and Faisal Othman shielding 20-year-old Ibrahim Ahmed Hussein between the sticks.

With eight goal involvements in his last nine matches for club and country, KFUM Oslo striker Nije is currently in fine form, and the 28-year-old striker should lead the Ocean Stars attack once again, while Mohamed Omar, Abdi Sharif and Mukhtar Suleiman should team up in midfield.

Ati-Zigi; Seidu, Adjetey, Salisu, Mensah; Partey, Yirenkyi; Kudus, Abdul Fatawu, Ayew; Thomas-Asante

Hussein; Mohamed, Gigli, A. Omar, Osman; M. Omar, Sharif, Suleiman; Addo, Njie, Hassan

Despite the quality in their rank, Ghana have failed an impression in the AFCON qualifiers so far, but victory on Thursday could provide the spark needed to turn their Group C campaign around.

Although Somalia have shown glimpses of their potential in their opening two matches, the difference in individual quality could prove a decisive factor here, with Ghana tipped to come away with all three points in front of their home supporters.

#1524. Premier League legend David Silva, 40, makes emphatic return to football with man-of-the-match performance - three and a half years after retiring

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 08:23 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 10:15 EST, 8 November 2026

David Silva made his mark in his first game since coming out of retirement after scoring on debut in a man-of-the-match display for Hong Kong outfit Sha Tin on Saturday.

Last month, the Manchester City icon revealed he was lacing his football boots in a professional sense again for the first time since 2023.

The 40-year-old started for Sha Tin and broke the deadlock against HK Rangers from the penalty spot in the 56th minute.

Silva stepped up and coolly passed the ball into the bottom left-hand corner - sending Hong Kong Rangers goalkeeper Ka-Yu Yip the wrong way.

The playmaker's goal sparked mass celebrations from his team-mates and the fans in the stands - with many taking their phones out of their pockets to record the moment.

However, Silva's debut didn't go as smoothly as planned as the visitors equalised in the 65th minute through Ibrahim Yakubu Nassam.

Some Spanish guy just scored a penalty for Sha Tin#DavidSilva #hkpl #hkfootball pic.twitter.com/JCbiYZEKE0

David Silva scored for Hong Kong outfit Sha Tin with this penalty in their 1-1 draw on Saturday

The 40-year-old celebrates with his team-mates after scoring against Hong Kong Rangers

Silva was named man-of-the-match, in what his first competitve match in over three years

With 11 minutes remaining, Silva was then booked before he was substituted in the 84th minute with his side down to 10 men following Maxwell Ansah's 81st-minute red card for a second bookable offence.

Despite failing to take all three points, Silva did collect the man-of-the-match award after the full-time whistle.

Sha Tin currently sit 10th in the Hong Kong Premier League with five points from their opening seven matches. They sit one point and place above bottom-placed Eastern AA, who occupy the sole relegation spot, and 14 points adrift of table-toppers North District.

Silva called it a day on his playing career back in 2023 when he tore his anterior cruciate ligament while playing for Real Sociedad.

He is most famed for spending ten years at Manchester City between 2010 and 2020, where he won 11 major honours; four Premier League titles, two FA Cups and five League Cups. Much of that time period, though, is now under scrutiny.

He also has a statue outside the Etihad Stadium, and won the 2010 World Cup with Spain, as well as Euro 2008 and Euro 2012.

Upon joining Sha Tin, ex-Valencia midfielder Silva said in an Instagram video: 'I'm so excited to go to Hong Kong and enjoy the local culture, the food in Sha Tin and, of course, football in Hong Kong.'

Silva will hope to lead his side to victory when they take on Southern District in the Hong Kong League Cup Losers play-offs on Saturday.
