#1506. Cesc Fabregas's Como win NINE-ONE in the biggest away victory in Champions League history - two weeks after thrashing Michael Carrick's Man United - in just their first year at Europe's top table

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR and LUKE POWER, SPORTS REPORTER

Published: 17:01 EST, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 17:59 EST, 8 November 2026

Manchester United's 4-1 battering by Como two weeks ago now looks a lucky escape – after the Italian side romped to a 9-1 victory at Lens in the Champions League.

Cesc Fabregas' side put in a stunning performance in a record-equalling win which well and truly announced them as contenders on the biggest stage.

Como now sit fourth in the Champions League standings after also thrashing RB Leipzig and Man United, who are likely relieved that Lens took such a pounding.

It means only Paris Saint-Germain, Real Madrid, and Arsenal have got off to better starts, despite this being their maiden season in European competition.

The lakeside outfit were 3-0 up at half-time – with the scorer of the third goal, Nico Paz, paying his respects to late Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel – before a rout after the break.

It is the latest statement win for Como, whose transformation began in 2019 when a pair of Indonesian billionaire brothers, who originally made their fortune in the tobacco industry, bought the club for $850,000 (£644,427) through their Djarum Group.

Como thrashed Lens 9-1 in a record-equalling victory in the Champions League on Wednesday

Cesc Fabregas is quickly building his name as one of the most talented coaches in Europe

With a combined net worth then estimated at $48billion (£36.4billion), Robert Budi Hartono and Michael Bambang Hartono instantly made Como the richest club in Italian football.

Rather than pursue instant success through lavish spending, Como have built steadily, investing in infrastructure, recruitment, and a clear footballing identity – and it is paying off big-time.

They have now won six games on the bounce, though they still sit fourth in Serie A five points behind leaders Lazio, who have had an almost perfect start.

Their crushing of Lens was the first time an Italian side had scored seven or more goals away from home in European Cup/Champions League history.

And their hat-trick hero on the night, Anastasios Douvikas, is now the top scorer in the Champions League ahead of Erling Haaland.

All of this comes for a side who were playing in the third tier just six seasons ago and on the back of a relatively modest summer spend of £58million on nine permanent arrivals and loanees.

'Today everything went our way,' said an ecstatic Fabregas post-match. 'A great night for Como and our fans.'

There was a poignant moment when Paz paid homage to Miguel and his hometown club, holding aloft a shirt with the picture of the late star alongside the caption: 'Rest in peace.' Though he plays for Argentina, Paz was born in Tenerife and also spent time in the club's youth system from 2014-16.

Miguel died on Tuesday morning less than 24 hours after a collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during their Spanish second division match on Monday. Having suffered serious head and chest injuries he subsequently suffered a cardiac arrest.

Como's Nico Paz paid tribute to Jesus de Miguel during his goalscoring celebration vs Lens

Despite playing for Argentina, Paz was born in Tenerife and also played for their youth teams

Tenerife striker De Miguel died on Tuesday morning after a horrifying clash with Jesus Owono

Como led 3-0 at half-time with hat-trick hero Douvikas scoring two at that point before Paz's goal and his De Miguel tribute.

Soon after the interval the Serie A outfit crushed any notion of the hosts coming back as they plundered in five goals in a devastating 22-minute spell which included Douvikas completing his hat-trick. Lucas Da Cunha, Marc-Oliver Kempf, Mattia Liberali, Martina Baturina also got in on the act during that period.

Ruben Aguilar pulled one back for Lens before Matteo Papaccioli rounded off the rout in stoppage time. The 18-year-old Papaccioli, who came on in the second half, is a member of Como's youth team and hasn't even played in Serie A yet.

Wednesday's win means Como have broken many records in the Champions League.

The Italian side matched the eight-goal winning margins recorded by Liverpool and Real Madrid in their 8-0 home victories over Besiktas and Malmo respectively. They also became only the second team after Bayern Munich to score nine goals in a Champions League match.

Como followed their 4-1 victory over Manchester United with another emphatic performance, becoming the first team to score nine goals away from home in the European Cup since 1971 – Feyenoord beat Olympiacos Nicosia by this scoreline – as they climbed to fourth in the standings on nine points. The previous best scoring performance by an away club in the Champions League was Bayern Munich's 8-2 win over Barcelona at a neutral venue (Lisbon) in 2020.

Fabregas's side may have made Champions League record-equalling history, but Feyenoord hold the European Cup mark for most goals scored in a single match, having beaten Icelandic side KR 12-2 in September 1969.

Lens, who suffered the heaviest defeat by a French club in the competition, are 33rd with three points.

#1504. Juventus Next Gen beaten 4-0 at Lecco and left third from bottom

Juventus Next Gen were beaten 4-0 at Lecco in Serie C Girone A, with three of the goals coming after half-time. Coach Massimo Brambilla admitted his young side give goals away too easily, and the table now reflects a long poor run.

At the Stadio Rigamonti-Ceppi, the manner of the defeat was as worrying as the scoreline.

The opener set the tone. Lecco needed only six minutes to go ahead. Casarotto ran through the middle, got past Corradi and beat goalkeeper Mangiapoco. Lecco held that single-goal lead until half-time.

Next Gen did have one clear opening before the break. In the 40th minute, Grelaud shot from near the penalty spot. Vettorel turned the effort over for a corner.

The second half was one-way traffic. Capello made it 2-0 in the 50th minute, and Manetti added a third in the 56th. Capello struck from close range after the goalkeeper parried Pellegrino’s second attempt. Murillo’s goal in the 72nd minute summed up the match. Mangiapoco erred as Juventus built from the back, and Murillo pounced.

The hosts are in strong form. This was their second 4-0 win in a row, after beating Dolomiti Bellunesi by the same score. Lecco have now scored 15 goals in four games.

Massimo Brambilla did not hide from the problems. He told TuttoMercatoWeb that his side struggled against Lecco’s high press. His players found it hard to keep the ball against a team pressing hard and man-to-man.

The coach also admitted that coming back became difficult after the second goal. He said his players must improve how they read the game and stop giving away goals so easily.

The table makes the warning sharper. Brambilla’s side sit third from bottom after the defeat, having won just one of their last 12 matches.

The result also matters beyond Serie C. Carnevali has put the youth sector at the centre of the club’s plans.

One player supporters will watch is Destiny Elimoghale, who came off the bench at Lecco. Next Gen had started in a 3-5-2, with Durmisi and Merola in attack. Elimoghale replaced Durmisi in the 40th minute of the second half. The forward was born in 2009. His new contract, announced on 3 November, runs until 30 June 2029.

Elimoghale was called up to the first-team squad for the first time on 17 September 2026. That call-up came for the opening Europa League league-phase match against NEC.

The next opponents arrive in good spirits. Treviso beat Novara 2-0 in round 13. Romeo scored in the 24th minute, and Paganini added the second in the 59th.

The next test comes quickly. Next Gen host Treviso in round 14 on Sunday 15 November at 17:30. A trip to Giana Erminio follows on Saturday 21 November, at the same kick-off time.

#1502. GdS: Tactics, data and team-mates – the ‘strange case’ of Goncalo Ramos at Milan

The Goncalo Ramos enigma continues to dominate the newspaper columns, as AC Milan try unlock their record signing.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport report, Milan fans hoped they had finally found a top-class striker in Ramos, but his three goals this season are not sufficient compared to expectations and the €70m price tag for which he arrived.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

And yet, the Portuguese centre-forward is still proving to be a factor in the team’s fortunes. The reason for this lies behind statistics that the average fan might ignore, but Ruben Amorim certainly isn’t.

The coach has repeatedly emphasised how Ramos is helping the team, less so the other way around. Looking at the numbers, you can’t argue with him. Gonçalo may not be making it into the top scorers’ table, but his work is well explained by statistics that place him among the top strikers in Serie A.

Which ones? Passes (20.7 per game, first in volume among centre-forwards in the league ahead of Lazio’s Noslin) or touches (2nd), for example. But also the aerial duels won and fouls drawn (19, first among attackers) underscore the importance of his sacrifice too.

There are two considerations that don’t emerge from the statistics, but are equally important. The first concerns the movements that free up or facilitate team-mates, such as the sprint for Milan’s first goal in Genoa.

Alphadjo Cisse found himself all alone in the penalty area thanks to Ramos drawing two of the Rossoblu central defenders towards him, allowing Adrien Rabiot to easily pass to the young Italian who was in lots of space.

The second consideration concerns the pressure and coverage work, which has changed since the start of the season. In the early days, Gonçalo was the first to apply pressure up front, but in doing so, he exposed Modric to too much space to cover in front of or behind him.

Amorim therefore asked the Portuguese to instead harass the opposing playmaker, without attacking the defence in the initial possession. This move allows Luka to run less and think more during the opponent’s possession phase.

We were talking about a Milan side that is helping Ramos less than the centre-forward is helping the team, too. The former Benfica man is 19th in Serie A for shots (26) and 15th for shots on target (10).

While it’s true that the Rossoneri maintain a high standard in terms of the quality of chances created (third in the league for big chances behind Inter and Roma), it’s equally undeniable that they arrive in the final third of the pitch less often than expected. Milan are 12th for touches in the opponent’s penalty area and 12th for shots on target.

In short, Ramos sees the ball mostly where he can’t hurt the goalkeepers. Even if, in relation to goal-scoring chances, he should have scored double in the league: 4.16 xG compared to the just two scored. Still, not enough for a Milan-calibre player.

#1497. Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under big pressure

This was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United. Not once. But twice. And, then, most painfully, a third time with a dismal, dispiriting defeat.

They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.

But then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals. And that was a far more painful and damaging blow.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy

On a day in which thousands of fans protested, accusing co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers – with Avram Glazer joining Ratcliffe in attendance – of treating them like “s---”, United unfortunately left a nasty whiff of being just that out on the pitch.

United were frankly, woeful. They lacked belief and imagination and attacking instinct and too many of their players – their apparent big players – went missing when they needed to stand up and take the game by the scruff of the neck. They could not break down City’s defence and failed to be a front-foot team who can dominate the ball. Which is surely what they aspire to be?

They hit the post twice – through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – with efforts from 25 yards. And those two local lads were by far their best players. Without them, United carried so little threat, were so blunt, that it was shocking.

The question for Michael Carrick, the Manchester United head coach, is simple: what is he trying to do with this team? Can they only ever depend on counter-attacks?

Afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical plan to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

It was telling that so little did City’s new head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their new head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

Was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a big team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

The former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

There was controversy around the red card and the goal. There is no doubt Foden had to go. But what about Fernandes? He clearly kicked Foden as he was on the ground with the midfielder reacting instinctively, two-footing him in the gut.

It meant he became the first City player to be dismissed in a Manchester derby in the league since Bernardo Corradi in December 2006 and will be punished with a three-match ban for violent conduct.

To make matters worse for Foden, who missed out on the World Cup, it happened in front of Thomas Tuchel who names his England squad for the Nations League campaign on Friday.

Phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL

And the goal? Initially it was ruled out for offside as Haaland superbly turned in Josko Gvardiol’s cross beyond the far post – he made that tricky finish look routine. But after a lengthy VAR check that decision was overturned by referee Michael Oliver.

Patrick Dorgu had played Haaland onside but the issue then was whether Fernández had touched the ball as he tried to reach the cross. He had not. But even if he had not, surely he was impeding Lisandro Martínez’s attempt to clear? He was certainly in the defender’s line of vision which fits the criteria for the offside to be given as it interfered with an opponent.

United can understandably complain but they can have no excuse. The pressure, already, will be beginning to mount on Carrick with just four points from four league games and down in 13th place. With a Carabao Cup tie at home to Brighton in midweek and a trip to Fulham next Sunday before the international break, he needs wins.

“We’ve only got 10 men,” goaded the City fans as the game headed into added time and United can expect to hear that again and again. And again.

Even so, at the death, Bryan Mbeumo – as otherwise anonymous as Matheus Cunha – had the chance to equalise after being shrewdly picked out by Fernandes. He was excellently thwarted by Gianluigi Donnarumma. But Mbeumo was clear inside the penalty area and had to score. Not that United would have deserved it. There were boos at the end and understandably so. United were just not good enough.

I’m confused. We put things in place in the game now. We have people in offices with all the screens for this decision. It’s more worrying about if that’s the interpretation of football now. If that’s the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that’s really worrying for me. It’s a staggering explanation.

The decision isn’t going to change the season, but it’s had a major impact on the game. That decision wasn’t on us today. It’s up to us to create and score after that. We had moments. Of course it’s up to us to do that, but big moments in games like that have a big impact.

We did a lot of things well, it looked like we were growing well into the game. We looked dangerous. We’ll take the positives from the game today and move on well, but we’re not moving on lightly.

We could have created more. That’s an answer for us, but we could have. That’s our second defeat now, since I’ve been in charge, but we’re a good team and we’ll get back to wining ways.

The red card changed the plan of the game but credit to the players because the effort, spirit and togetherness has been brilliant.

[On Foden’s red card] Can be a red card, but in the same action can be a red card for Bruno. It is what it is, we won.

Changed the plan for us, and changed the plan for them. They are unbelievable in transition, and the moment we are with 10 men we give them no transitions.

When you are able to win a game with 10 players it’s fantastic, when this game is a derby it’s even better.

Last year with Chelsea I had a player sent off here after three minutes, this year 25, hopefully next time we play against 11vs11!

We always knew it was going to be a tough game. What happened with Phil at the start wasn’t good for us, but we said at half-time it would make us feel better if we win and we’ve taken three points.

It just gives you more motivation to go on and get the points. It was really tough for us. We had to run more and fight more. We all shone, to a man, and we were brilliant.

He was offside and what I can’t understand is it’s the rules... I went there because he was in front of him because that’s why Haaland was free at the back.

Every season they come to our club and spend an hour and a half explaining the rules, and they seem so confident with that, and then you have five or six people making this mistake. It’s unacceptable.

Haaland speaking on Sky: “We had to go low which is not ideal, we like to keep the ball, to try to score goals but in these times you have to go a bit low and take your chances when possible. We managed to do that well and that shows personality and character, to keep the ball away at Old Trafford with 10 men.”

“We had to change the plan a bit, but Enzo gave us a plan where we could play to our different strengths and counter-attack a bit more. For me personally, I just had to be there, to try to wait for a chance, and if there’s a chance, I had to be ready to execute. We also needed fighters in the team, which we have plenty of. Look at our midfield - it’s something they like to do! I’m so, so proud of everyone.”

And on Donnarumma’s late save: “This wolf in goal giving you so much confidence, he looks a bit like a wolf. He is a mad man but he is a match-winner as well.”

9 - Erling Haaland is now the top scorer in Premier League games between Manchester City and Manchester United:9 - Haaland (8 apps)8 - Agüero (13 apps)8 - Rooney (21 apps)Domination. pic.twitter.com/EBiifV12st

City win the Old Trafford derby with 10 men and Enzo Maresca runs down the touchline to celebrate in front of the travelling fans while their players embrace Donnarumma after his late save.

There will be so much analysis of Foden’s red card, but more so how Haaland’s winner stood given the final result. Should Enzo Fernandez have been considered offside?

But if you are judging performances, City are worthy winners. They defended stoutly, carried a threat and kept the ball well for periods even though they were a man light. United were aimless and froze.

A mammoth victory, and one which perhaps puts the breaks on talk of an Arsenal procession.

What a chance for Mbeumo to equalise! Superb save by Donnarumma, after the United forward was found by a Bruno Fernandes disguised pass into the box. Mbeumo took the ball under his spell and shot with power, but the big goalkeeper pushed the shot over the bar.

United have a corner, but Michael Oliver blows for a foul, and that is surely that.

Martinez tries a straight ball towards Sesko, which is too high for the striker. United have perhaps just one more attack in them if they are too salvage a point.

Dalot with another poor cross that flies over everyone in the penalty area. Then Mainoo’s pass in midfield is intercepted by Anderson, and Ndiaye can bring the ball forward for City until he his tackled buy Martinez.

Fernandes drifts a cross behind for a City goal kick, between Sesko and Zirkzee and it looks like United are running out of time and ideas.

Dorgu with another foul on Ndiaye, yet another break in play for City. And there are going to just FIVE minutes of added time, much to Old Trafford’s frustration.

Haaland does well to bring City forward after another United attack breaks down, and Dorgu is penalised for a foul on Ndiaye. Another stoppage follows because the ball hits Michael Oliver. City can see the finish line so, and they would deserve their three points.

United have a corner after Guehi stands firm to block Cunha’s strike from distance. Maguire rises highest in the middle, but no United player gambled on the knockdown and his header drifts wide of the post.

Good work from Anderson against Mainoo in midfield, he receives a big cheer from the City fans. Carrick has thrown attackers on, but United have lost some structure and are not sustaining pressure.

Nico O’Reilly is now on for the closing stages, in place of Fernandez and Carrick has thrown on Zirkzee in place of Marcus Rashford. A United goal now would feel like a goal out of nowhere. City are playing the better football now and they have a corner.

United have lost all sense of momentum, City are keeping the ball for spells and then are happy for the game to be broken up stoppages.

Fernandez goes down looking for a penalty rather hopefully, and Maguire has been booked for his reaction as well as Fernandez for his role in the fracas. More and more time ticks away.

City are showing real resolve as well as quality here, Enzo Fernandez has just won a free-kick in the United half after a foul by Mainoo. The closest United have come in recent minutes was a glancing header wide from Mbeumo.

From that free-kick, Fernandez’s low delivery is close to being converted by Haaland or Guehi.

It’s a big final 16 minutes here plus injuries for United. You’re at home to your derby rivals who have been down to 10 men since the 23rd minute and you’ve had just two players show up for the mostpart so far - Mainoo and Rashford. The rest are really going to have to lift it.

Fernandes stings the palms of Donnarumma with a strike from outside the box.

We have now had an explanation and evidence of why the goal stood. The VAR check for offside on Haaland found that he was in fact onside by fine margins, and that Fernandez (who was offside) did not affect Lisandro Martinez as he threw himself at a diving header (and missed). The Fernandez element feels the more debatable.

#MUNMCI – 59' VAR OVERTURNVAR checked the referee's call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded.The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn't play the ball. pic.twitter.com/TyTip3ACIh

Enzo Fernandes’s shot from the edge of the D is tipped on to the post by Lammens! United are living dangerously, and Carrick has now thrown Sesko on in place of Tielemans.

Sesko on for United. Surprised he’s not come on before. City fans singing “Enzo, he’s in your head, Enzo, Enzo” to the tune of the Cranberries’ Zombie – and then he goes and hits a post.

What a final 30 minutes or so of football we have in store now. There will be an air of panic spreading through the United ranks, and Haaland, Ndiaye and Semenyo are still posing a threat.

Haaland and his City team-mates run off to celebrate in front of the away fans including Noel Gallagher.

The goalscorer looked marginally ahead of Dorgu and offside, but the camera angles can deceive. The reasoning for the final decision is not entirely clear.

United fans were goading and laughing at their City counterparts when the goal was initially ruled out for offside but it’s City who have had the last laugh.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy

Sky are saying that VAR has concluded the striker is in an “onside position”.

It looks like they might be checking the position of Enzo Fernandez in the middle.

Haaland has the ball in the net but the flag is up for offside! Great finish at the back post from Gvardiol’s cross, but the City striker had just strayed offside. There is an ongoing VAR check, though.

City with a better sequence of passing but it does Ndiaye cannot get a shot away and then Fernandez commits another foul in midfield. Cunha with a poor cross behind for a City goal kick.

Bryan Mbeumo with a wild shot over the bar after cutting inside from the right, Mainoo was involved in propelling United forward once again. Then Cunha shoots over from a tight angle, but United are knocking on the door now.

Much better from United in the last few minutes, the crowd are engaged again and possibly for the first time in the game it feels like a goal might be coming. Nice idea from Rashford to let the ball run to Dorgu but the left-back is offside.

Kobbie Mainoo hits the post! Lovely strike from 25 yards after a Dalot pull-back is flicked into his path by Fernandes. Plenty of whip on it, and Donnarumma was beaten all ends up. Then United are back at the heart of the City defence, but Rashford’s shot deflects behind for a corner, from which the City goalkeeper is fouled.

He’s been United’s best player by a distance so far this season and Kobbie Mainoo goes very close there to giving United the lead with a fine strike that hits the post. Next passage of play and he releases Rashford in on the left whose shot is pushed out for a corner.

Kobbie Mainoo was INCHES from opening the scoring against Manchester United 🤏 pic.twitter.com/l9v8mlxzk3

Haaland does well to win City a free-kick in the United half after rolling Martinez. City had an early United corner to defend but they did so well. Quite a slow tempo to the game all round.

Fernandez’s deep delivery finds the unmarked Dias, and his header deflects behind for a City corner. Maguire heads away, and then Anderson’s cross drifts behind for a goal kick.

Strange moment as the game kicks-off while Sky’s Patrick Davison is still talking to Michael Carrick. He signs off in almost apologetic fashion for distracting the United manager from his job.

Ndiaye on for Cherki, so Maresca opting for a player who can dribble the ball over long distances.

Keane said: “For me, Fernandes is the player who has been violent. I don’t think that is a red card for Foden. Foden is a bit daft, but so is Bruno.”

Micah Richards said: “Because Foden doesn’t react in terms of, when he got kicked (by Fernandes) and started screaming on the floor, Fernandes would have been sent off. The fact Fernandes, as soon as he has touched him and there is minimal touching.. If Foden starts screaming the decision is reversed. As soon as Foden touches him Fernandes is screaming and rolling about the floor. Of course it (Foden kick) looks worse than it is. But I agree with Roy, Fernandes kicks him. As a player of course you are going to have some sort of reaction, I don’t agree with Foden’s reaction but Fernandes started it.”

🗣️ "Bruno [Fernandes] is the one who is violent here, I have to call it out"Roy Keane doesn't believe Phil Foden deserved to be sent off against Man Utd 🟥 pic.twitter.com/up5ZQqFShy

This fixture has often brought out the best in Phil Foden but this is a third successive visit to Old Trafford he will want to forget. He was substituted at half-time of the 2-0 defeat in January with a broken hand and the season before he had been withdrawn before the hour mark after a poor performance in a 0-0 draw. And now sent off after 24 minutes.

A half that will be remembered for one thing and one thing only: Phil Foden’s red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.

United were shading things before that flashpoint, but City will be pleased with their response to the sending off. They have defended well, and posed a threat going forward without executing the final pass or shot.

This is now a different game to the one United were expecting, so perhaps Carrick needs to shuffle the pack.

United win a free-kick about 25 yards from goal after Enzo Fernandez chases his own poor touch and fouls Tielemans.

Rashford to take... cracking hit, up and over the wall but the attempt bounces wide off the post.

United struggling to carve out clear openings, nobody was planning for the game to have this pattern with the home team dominating possession and City dropping off into a deep defensive shape. Nunes does exceptionally well to win a tackle, drive out from the back and find Cherki.

City threaten again after a poor defensive header by Dalot, with Semenyo fizzing in a low cross that is deflected behind for a corner with Fernandez lurking in the six-yard box. United have lost their way in the last 10 minutes, Dalot flagged offside unnecessarily.

There’s a reminder of City’s threat: Haaland spinning a pass wide right to Cherki who is in acres, but with Haaland in the middle and Semenyo on the edge of the box he crosses to nobody at the back stick.

He was not a starter in Carrick’s original game plan, but I wonder if United’s task now calls for Benjamin Sesko and some extra penalty-box presence and aerial threat. Guehi is having a very sound game at the back for City.

Both teams adjusting after the red card, Cherki and Semenyo are trying to put in a defensive shift in front of their full-backs. United enjoying the majority of possession, and Fernandes feeds Rashford with a delightful reverse pass but Rashford’s first touch was loose.

United will now be favourites to win this game, but Mainoo was required to block a goal-bound strike from Cherki after a corner was clear. City do have the ammunition to offer a threat on the break. They need the Haaland of his Dortmund days to attack big spaces on the counter.

Old Trafford is delirious because United’s scourge in so many derbies is off for an early shower. Fernandes and Foden were scrapping for the ball near the touchline, the United man had a nibble at Foden as he tried to protect the ball. But then Foden kicked up from the ground with his studs into the midriff of Fernandes. I don’t think he can have any complaints.

Although Foden’s sending off will certainly not have enhanced his prospects! Kicking out in retaliation at being kicked by Bruno Fernandes when he was on the ground.

Phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL

The Old Trafford crowd are encouraged by what they are watching, but Enzo Fernandez takes some of the venom from their attacking momentum by winning a foul.

Then Ruben Dias clips a long ball forward over Dalot’s head which the right-back makes a mess of to Semenyo’s benefit, but the winger finds the gloves of Lammens with the cross. Just had to clear the goalkeeper and Haaland would have had an open goal.

England manager Thomas Tuchel and his assistant Anthony Barry are among those in attendance at Old Trafford ahead of Friday’s squad announcement, the first since the World Cup and ahead of the forthcoming Nations League campaign. There are plenty of players on show, on both sides ,who will hope to be in contention including Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford for United although Harry Maguire may have talked his way out of being considered after his reaction to not making the World Cup squad. For City there is Marc Guehi and Elliot Anderson - who both will be included - and it feels like a big game for Phil Foden.

Very wasteful from Haaland, after Bruno Fernandes’s stray wall pass back into midfield ran into his path. Neither picked a pass nor let fly with a shot and lost control of the ball.

At the other end, Guehi defends well against Rashford and City have a goal kick, but United have the upper hand in the game at the moment.

Cunha with a burst through City’s midfield and he is brought down by Fernandez. Just before that, City invited the pressure with a stray cross-field pass in their own defensive third which Guehi could not control. Mainoo then whips a teasing cross to the back post, but Rashford misread the flight of it and he was offside in any case.

City with a more sustained spell of possession in the United half, but Martinez defends well as Foden dribbles into the penalty area. Cunha then tries to release Rashford behind the City defence, but Dias covered well behind Guehi to intercept.

Promising counter-attack for United after Rashford pinches the ball off Foden in midfield, and the home team’s attacking quartet of players stream forward. Poor from Cunha though, dragging a shot well wide from an improbable distance.

Quite a composed start from City, Anderson enjoying plenty of touches in midfield. Fernandes tries to sweep a first-time pass out to Rashford wide left, but Nunes intercepts.

Then Fernandes’s next pass is more threatening, lofting a pass over the City defence for the run of Diogo Dalot but he cannot quite put the ball under his spell in the penalty area.

Rashford finds himself near the right touchline and finds room to drive inside with the ball, where he is sandwiched between Semenyo and Anderson. Free-kick for United in a crossing position right of centre, and from the second phase a Martinez cross flies into the gloves of Donnarumma.

An early glimpse of United’s slightly flimsy central midfield with Cherki finding space behind them and Enzo Fernandez’s strike from distance deflecting over the bar. Martinez heads Anderson’s delivery behind for another corner.

This time City take it short, but United clear their lines when the ball is crossed into the box.

The ball changes hands in midfield a couple of times in quick succession. Dalot pressing Semenyo but the winger gets away from him, but United win a challenge before Anderson nips in. Promising start if you want aggression and intensity.

Maguire is then penalised for a foul on Cherki in a more promising position for City, but from a free-kick taken short the flag goes up for offside. City claim there was a foul on Cherki from Fernandes.

United get the first Manchester derby of the season under way.

As expected, there is that banner above the mouth of the tunnel.

“THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE” banner is displayed above the Munich tunnel on the south west corner of the Stretford End.

Avram Glazer is in the directors’ box with Sir Jim Ratcliffe behind his co-owner.

"THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE" banner above the tunnel#MUFC pic.twitter.com/hrs71K7r1y

Probably keeping the emotions away, which is not easy. It’s just try to embrace the chaos, that’s it..

I say chaos, [but] it can be noise. Embrace it, it’s a derby, it’s nice... Try to play our game!

We’ve got a lot of encouragement going into the season, of course we wanted more points at this stage. We understand how important this game is and what it can do but it’s getting the balance, we know it’s a long season and we have to be consistent over a period of time. In some ways everything is on today, and it has to be, but it’s not everything in terms of the bigger picture.

Michael Carrick’s record has been outstanding, particularly at Old Trafford. They’ve been brilliant here and very difficult to beat.

If United drop points today, people will say it’s a bad start, if they win today, people will say they’re back.

If you had read Sam Wallace’s exclusive interview with United’s right-back you would know he was in line to make his 250th appearance for the club. Dalot did not want to take Carrick’s team selection for granted when talking about the milestone, but United’s manager is not replete with full-back options.

Some supporters also targeted ambitions to build a new 100,000 capacity stadium adjacent to Old Trafford by singing: “You can shove your new ground up your a---.”

Inside Old Trafford, all flags in the Stretford End are set to be removed with and replaced by one banner that reads: “THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE.”

Struck by the nature of both midfields. If you look over the careers of Anderson-Fernandez-Cherki and Tielemans-Mainoo-Fernandes, Anderson is the only player of the six who has not played as a No 10 or advanced midfielder. The other five are not especially adept at covering ground and defensive actions, so this could well be wide open.

Thousands of Manchester United fans have been marching in protest at the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s running of the club.

Supporters have reacted with outrage to the club’s handling of a controversial anti ticket touting operation they felt unfairly singled out innocent fans.

And thousands have taken to the streets to voice their anger at how they feel they are being treated by the co-owners.

Plumes of red and green and yellow smoke filled the air as fans brandished banners and flags and chanted anti-Glazer and Ratcliffe songs.

“You take it all from fans and banning us for nothing. Premium prices all for greed,” read one banner.

One banner is a Stones Roses-themed number emblazoned with “Jim Aint The One”, a nod to Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the song This Is The One which is played at Old Trafford as the teams emerge from the tunnel.

Enzo Maresca has selected the more attacking option by playing Enzo Fernandez deeper alongside Elliot Anderson, rather than pushing the Argentine up a line and starting O’Reilly or Bouaddi. Still no Doku for City, and Foden has been preferred to Ndiaye out wide.

It is a very offensive-minded XI with Dorgu at full-back and a midfield trio of Tielemans, Fernandes and Mainoo behind Mbeumo, Cunha and Rashford. The results could be spectacular, but City should fancy punching holes in that set up.

Representing the Reds on derby day... 📋❤️‍🔥COME ON UNITED! 🗣️🗣️🗣️

They are now 2-0 down against Brighton and Taiwo Awoniyi has been sent off for an elbow. Bar a miracle, it will be zero points from four games for Frank Lampard’s team.

There will be no flags in the Stretford End today in a protest against ticketing policy which United say is about stopping touts, but loyal, innocent fans may have been caught in the crossfire. A crackdown has led to 685 supporters being stripped of their season tickets and another 464 being sanctioned. Fans will unfurl a giant banner reading “The Way You Treat Us Is A Disgrace” aimed at the club’s hierarchy this afternoon. You can read more here from James Ducker.

"You can shove your new ground up your a*rse"#MUFC protests pic.twitter.com/EMmnF8FhNo

Kostoulas has given Brighton the lead away at Coventry, who are still to pick up their first Premier League point. Around five minutes until half-time in that one. It was quite some finish.

"What an outstanding finish, absolutely brilliant!"Charalampos Kostoulas fires Brighton in front with a wonderful finish 💥 pic.twitter.com/bMKJACr2bd

Both of these teams were in Champions League action this week but, as James Ducker explores in this piece, United have missed out in six of the last 13 campaigns. City have been ever-presents, with significant sporting and financial benefits. Over the 10 years between 2016 and 2025, City generated £343m more in broadcast revenue and prize money from European football than their derby rivals.

Sam Wallace was at Carrington this week to speak with Diogo Dalot, the Manchester United right-back who could make his 250th appearance for the club this afternoon. Dalot has been through some tumultuous times at Old Trafford, and is one of the great survivors in the squad. He talks about the scrutiny at United, his musical family and the negatives of social media for young players in an interview you can read here.

My sense is that while United fans generally understand and agree with the decision to stick with Carrick, they hope he is the long-term answer to get the club back to winning the Premier League or Champions League, while the rest of the world doubts it.

To most, it feels like Carrick remains an interim solution in all but name, entrusted with the keys to Old Trafford until a super coach can move in during the summer of 2027. Carrick will not see it that way, of course, but there are certain perceptions which will be tough to shake off.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the season’s first Manchester derby, with midfield rebuilds the theme of the summer on both sides of town.

Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi could all be involved for City, who lost Rodri and Bernardo Silva in the engine room, while United have recruited Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in an attempt to address a long-standing problem.

Rodri’s departure and a Community Shield shellacking by Arsenal prompted some gloomy forecasts for Enzo Maresca and City, but confidence has grown since. The late turnaround at home to Bournemouth on the opening weekend could well look very important in a few months’ time, while Crystal Palace and Coventry have also been put away. Victory in Porto was probably Maresca’s most impressive result to date at City, though winning at Old Trafford would usurp that. Three points for City would mean they join Arsenal on a maximum of 12 points from four games.

It has been a patchy start to the campaign for United and Michael Carrick, and this afternoon’s result will go a long way to shaping perceptions of where they are. The concession of a late equalise at Everton, in addition to a dreadful loss at Hull, adds a degree of pressure. United will be buoyed by their performance in this fixture in January, when they delivered possibly the best performance of the post-Ferguson years to slay City in a 2-0 win that could well have been four or five.

With Tielemans, Bruno Fernandes and Kobbie Mainoo prominent in midfield, United are trying to shift to a more possession-heavy approach, but any success against City in recent times has tended to come on the counter-attack. Maresca’s team have had lots of the ball in their first few games of the season, so that is the expected pattern again.Full team news on the way later.

#1496. Repubblica: Milan and Real Madrid watching as Napoli star McTominay stalls on contract

Scott McTominay’s Napoli future is in doubt, and a report has named AC Milan among the surprise potential suitors.

In a Napoli side that appears to have lost its way, one of the few lights leading the way remains McTominay. Despite a season that started on the wrong foot and a heart condition (now resolved), the Scot has five goals in 11 games this season across Serie A and the Champions League.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Massimiliano Allegri’s team is going through a tough time, and the former Manchester United player himself has had some tough nights. As La Repubblica (via Calciomercato.com) report, Napoli fans are beginning to worry about where things are heading.

The 29-year-old McTominay is at a turning point in his career, one which has been revitalised since his arrival at Napoli and the Scudetto won under Antonio Conte. His current contract with the Neapolitans expires in 2028, but negotiations for a renewal have stalled.

Fabrizio Romano reported that Napoli remain confident in the possibility of reaching an agreement over an extension, but the uncertainty currently surrounding the project, the bad results and doubts about the club’s future are forcing him to evaluate.

La Repubblica add that the discussions have even stalled after positive steps were taken in September. McTominay and his representatives want to better understand the Azzurri’s vision moving forward before finalising a new agreement.

Sky Switzerland journalist Sacho Tavolieri reported that the former Manchester United man’s agent has already held discussions with several English clubs. Napoli have not completely ruled out a possible sale, and the figure would be €25-30m.

His contract is currently worth €4.5m net per season. Napoli would like to extend it until 2030 with a salary increase, but they are unwilling to accept the Scotsman’s demands, who has requested around €7-8m net per season.

According to La Repubblica, at the end of the season McTominay and Napoli will sit down to discuss the terms of the new contract, once the club’s plans are clearer. Several clubs are interested though and are watching closely.

Aston Villa and Manchester United enquired in the summer. In the coming weeks, Real Madrid and AC Milan will also be keeping a close eye on the developments surrounding McTominay.

The Rossoneri are currently well-stocked in midfield with Luka Modric, Adrien Rabiot, Yunus Musah, Ardon Jashari plus options like Ruben Loftus-Cheek and the young Christian Comotto. However, with Amorim at the helm, the prospect of profound change is never far away.

They’re very similar players, but Rabiot is slightly better defensively and Scotty Mac is slightly better offensively. Add a quick defensive midfielder next to Rabiot and we’re cooking with gas. Rabiot with a top DM in the pivot, and Pulisic with McTominay behind the striker is a scudetto midfield.

“Well-stocked in midfield” but with what? Modric (41, retiring) Rabiot, Musah (it’s Musah) Jashari (so far pretty useless) Loftus-Cheek (somehow escaped the bomb squad) and Comotto (haven’t seen him play but clearly out of favor)…

#1495. French team: when Pablo Pagis learns of his first selection

Zinedine Zidane unveiled his second list as coach of the France team this Friday. Among ZZ’s many decisions, one choice particularly attracts attention: Pablo Pagis (23 years old). The Paris Football Club attacking midfielder will receive his very first call-up to the Blues in the coming days, taking advantage of Maghnes Akliouche’s package. The reaction of the principal concerned was not long in coming.

It was on the Paris FC bus, which was traveling to Auxerre for the match between the two teams in Ligue 1, that Pagis learned of his call-up to the Blues alongside his teammates. The former Lorient player was warmly congratulated by his teammates as well as his coach, Liam Ronsenior. Arriving this summer at the Ile-de-France club, Pagis has two goals and an assist in nine games this season.

#1494. Some are calling this 'Tuchel 2.0' and his latest squad does feel like that. Here's why England think a tilt at the European Championship is within reach, writes IAN LADYMAN

Published: 17:35 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 05:45 EST, 9 November 2026

One of Thomas Tuchel’s favourite analogies when it comes to the development of his England team is that of a train leaving a station with only the chosen few on it. As time moves on, the bodies lying on the tracks are growing greater in number.

Consider this statistic. Of the 26 players who travelled to the World Cup in America 13 are not in the squad chosen by England manager Tuchel for next week’s Nations League games against Croatia and Spain. And that does not include Cole Palmer and Phil Foden who, after missing out in the summer, were expected by many of us to have forced a way back in by now.

Tuchel’s latest selection has been affected by injuries, of course. But more significant is that the experienced German believes he is now starting to see an England team and squad develop in a way and in a direction that even he hadn’t envisaged once Argentina ended his World Cup hopes in that dismal Atlanta semi-final in July.

Different feelings, different style of play and, to a degree, different players.

Some are calling this ‘Tuchel 2.0’ and it does feel a little bit like that. The start of the second phase of Tuchel’s tenure, the start of the road towards a tilt at another trophy, the European Championships of 2028.

Having admitted to some worry ahead of the four-game international break FIFA saddled us all with last month, Tuchel sat down yesterday looking and sounding like a man once again certain of himself.

Tuchel sat down with the media looking and sounding like a man once again certain of himself

The inclusion of Jobe Bellingham — Jude’s younger brother (right) — was the headline act but there were other messages written within

Certain enough of a direct, quick, athletic style of play that helped England to two wins over Czech Republic and one – by seven goals – against Croatia in Rijeka. And certain that a dependence on players like Jordan Henderson, Dan Burn and John Stones for what we may politely call ‘squad culture management’ lies now in the past.

All of this may crash down in Madrid next Sunday. Spain have already beaten Tuchel’s England once – at Wembley in late September – and a repeat this month would ask familiar questions about England against the really good teams.

But for now, Tuchel is confident enough to claim that he has found his path.

‘We said at some point we need to take the next step, to build on what we have, to get better and to improve otherwise you’re just left behind,’ said Tuchel yesterday.

‘That’s how football works. You have been champion in one season but you need to improve, you need to bring in new players for competition, young players, new energy, fresh energy. It’s also the way, naturally, the national team goes.

‘We cannot be stuck in the same personnel and in the same style of play.

‘I agreed with you last month. I was the first to admit I was not 100 per cent happy with the pure level of football we played in the US. I saw a higher level in training [than on the field], I saw a higher level in glimpses.

‘We adjusted some things tactically, created some new positions and took the next steps.’

The Tuchel we sat down with in late September still wore the scars of the summer’s disappointment – and the criticism that came with it – rather visibly. It was the first time we had seen him like that in his two years in the job. He was tetchy and easily provoked. Call it the Argentina effect if you like.

Here, he appeared rather healed. Good results tend to do that for a manager and a little time helps too. If he believes his team has moved on then maybe he has also and he had to.

Certainly, his selection squad speaks to that. The inclusion of Jobe Bellingham – Jude’s younger brother – was the headline act but there were other messages written within.

Henderson and Burn are available but not included. So too Arsenal’s Noni Madueke, excluded to the benefit of the more direct Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha.

‘We need runners who will go between the lines,’ said Tuchel. A clear indication, there, that too much of England’s summer wing play was too slow and too conservatively narrow.

Palmer, Foden and Kobbie Mainoo are also on the outside looking in once again and the case of the Manchester United midfielder is perhaps indicative of how Tuchel now operates.

Moved to apologise to him in front of the whole squad in July for his lack of minutes at the World Cup, Tuchel was determined Mainoo would play in the opening four games of the Nations League campaign.

‘I was desperate to give him the minutes and desperate to include him in this new start,’ explained Tuchel.

‘But then he pulled out. He missed an excellent camp and also entered a difficult, difficult spell for himself.

‘Man United fell off a cliff a little bit performance-wise. So this is why he now suffers.’

We can talk about the whys and wherefores of that logic. If Mainoo was good enough in September then why is he not good enough now? How desperate could Tuchel really have been to play him that one withdrawal with injury closed the door for the next camp and opened it instead for Bellingham jnr?

This, though, is how Tuchel works. He is an adept tactician but he’s also a mood coach, someone who – after sobering club experiences at places like PSG, Chelsea and Bayern Munich – places huge emphasis on environments and gut feels and culture. If he feels something works, he doesn’t like to pick it apart without good reason.

This is why for example the growing voice and influence of Elliot Anderson has left Jordan Henderson suddenly surplus. Tuchel says the door is not closed on a player who will be 38 by the time the next Euros are played and he called him this week to say so. In Tuchel’s mind, though, England will now move without the veteran and others of his ilk.

‘I was concerned before the last camp that we missed the players who kept our standards,’ said Tuchel.

‘I was worried that we missed so many of them. But then this group found their own way and their own voices.

It’s also reasonable to ask why our head coach can’t find room in his squad – if not his team – for the game changing duo of Palmer and Foden

‘I know what the others did. They built a platform on which these ones can build.’

Time will tell. To a degree, Spain will tell. Can England play the kind of higher tempo, front foot football we saw against Croatia and the Czechs against the world and European champions next Sunday? They embarrassed us when we didn’t have the ball at Wembley.

It’s also reasonable to ask why our head coach can’t find room in his squad – if not his team – for the game-changing duo of Palmer and Foden. England lacked good substitutes at the World Cup. There was too much like for like.

England need to win in order for such decisions to be vindicated and Tuchel knows that.

Asked yesterday if he felt as invigorated as he looked he said he did. ‘The last camp gave me a lot of energy, gave me a lot of extra belief,’ he said.

‘It gave me a lot of optimism to not compromise on the way England teams should play. Be physical but also step up in the pure level of performances.’

It’s certainly time for this now. The summer only served to expose English shortcomings. Tuchel’s train must arrive in Madrid next weekend, not only with fresh personnel but also new ideas clearly apparent.

#1493. Liberali praises Cisse and looks back on Milan decision: “It wasn’t easy”

Mattia Liberali has looked back on his decision to leave AC Milan and to snub rejoining them, insisting he has ‘no regrets’.

After making his way through the youth sector, Liberali burst onto the scene in the 2024 summer preseason under Paulo Fonseca. He also made his first senior start under the Portuguese coach, but then found chances hard to come by and opted to leave the following year.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

On Tuesday afternoon, Liberali spoke in the press conference room at Coverciano – the Italian national team headquarters – alongside Alphadjo Cisse. The pair were team-mates at Catanzaro last season and could have reunite at Milan, but the former chose to head to Cesc Fabregas’ Como.

Speaking to the reporters present, Liberali once again commented on why he wanted to leave Milan in the first place to head to the Serie B side. His words were relayed by MilanNews.

Is there any regret about how things ended with Milan?

“No regrets. You have to make decisions with confidence and not look back. I’m very happy for Cisse, who’s succeeding. It wasn’t easy leaving AC Milan, but it’s always important to look forward.”

What was it like making the jump to Como?

“It’s not easy to go from Serie B to the intensity of Serie A and the Champions League. Aquilani? I’m sorry about his dismissal, he helped me so much last year. I’ll write to him in the next few days, I’m sorry he wasn’t able to make his mark at Sassuolo.”

#1492. In vivo CAR-T double knockout screen maps synergistic antitumour gene pairs

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed the treatment of haematological malignancies, but its efficacy remains limited by multiple negative regulatory mechanisms intrinsic to T cells1,2,3,4. Here we perform a high-throughput in vivo CAR-T double-knockout (DKO) CRISPR screen, and identify multiple DKO gene pairs that are both effective and synergistic. The top pair, NR4A1–SOCS3 DKO, has multiple favourable immunological features. Whole-transcriptome profiling and in vivo single-cell RNA sequencing reveal that NR4A1–SOCS3 DKO specifically upregulates metabolic pathways in CAR-T cells, which show significantly higher metabolic fitness and mitochondrial activity. NR4A1–SOCS3 DKO CAR-T cells and T cells exhibit exceptionally potent antitumour efficacy and long-term tumour control across different tumour models without compromising safety features. NR4A1–SOCS3 DKO outperforms several benchmark single-gene and dual-gene modifications in T cells and CAR-T cells5,6,7,8,9. These data demonstrate high-throughput in vivo CAR-T DKO screening for rapid discovery of combination targets, and establish NR4A1–SOCS3 as a promising pair of intracellular checkpoints to engineer high-performance CAR-T therapies against cancer.

a, Quantification of CD3− cells 5 days after CRISPR-mediated gene editing in three independent donors. b, Quantification of live cells 5 days after editing with the indicated Cas9 mRNA concentrations, n = 3 biologically independent replicates. Data are shown as mean + s.e.m. Significance was calculated using one-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s multiple-comparisons test. ns, not significant. c, Left, representative flow cytometry plots showing CD3 and CD28 protein-level DKO efficiency in activated human primary T cells 5 days after Cas9 mRNA electroporation. Right, quantification of CD3+ CD28+ cells in DKO and vector control groups; data are shown as mean + s.e.m.; n = 4 infection replicates. Significance was calculated using a paired two-sided t-test, ****P < 0.0001. d, Quantification of CD3− or CD28− cells 5 days after editing; n = 3 donors per concentration. Data are shown as mean ± s.e.m. e, Classification and composition of targeted genes in the T cell DKO CRISPR library. f, Schematic of the two-step T cell DKO CRISPR library construction process. g, Quantification of plasmid library sgRNA-pair construct distribution. h, Flow cytometry histograms showing EGFRvIII expression in U87-GL and U87-GL-EGFRvIII cell lines. i, Flow cytometry histograms showing PD-L1 expression in U87-GL and U87-GL-EGFRvIII cell lines. j, Schematic of DKO CAR-T cell library generation pipeline, including human T cell isolation and activation, CAR-T cell generation and selection, lentiviral DKO CRISPR library infection and Cas9 mRNA electroporation. Schematic in panel j created in BioRender; Chen, S. https://biorender.com/4g9xapi (2026). k, Spider plots of tumour volumes for donor 1 in vivo screen experiment shown in Fig. 1d. n = 5 biologically independent mice. l, Representative H&E-stained tumour sections from two biologically independent tumours per group from the screen shown in Fig. 1c. Scale bar, 250 μm. m, sgRNA-pair detection rates from the total library across individual samples. D, donor; T, tumour. n, Heat map of Spearman correlation coefficients between the log2-normalized counts-per-million (log-norm.) sgRNA counts for each sample. Data were arranged by hierarchical clustering using the ward.D2 method. o, Multidimensional scaling analysis of log2-normalized screen data using the top 10,000 most variable sgRNA pairs across samples. Data points were clustered by k-means. p, Box-dot plot of library representation across individual samples, showing the distribution of all sgRNA-pair constructs counts. Boxes indicate the 25th–75th percentiles, center lines indicate medians, and whiskers extend to the most extreme values within 1.5 times the interquartile range. Individual points represent sgRNA-pair counts. q, Empirical cumulative distribution function of DKO library representation among detected sgRNA pairs in plasmid, pre-injection cell and tumour samples. Sample labels in m-p indicate sample type, plasmid, pre-injection cell or tumour, and donor ID.

a, Distribution of the top four performing sgRNA-pair constructs for top DKO hits across samples, ranked by SAMBA sgRNA z-score. b, Heat map of DKO screen scores for all pairwise gene combinations assessed in the CRISPR screen. Values were scaled and visualized within a range of −1 to 1. Hierarchical clustering was performed using the Ward.D2 method based on Euclidean distances. c, Scatter plot showing the relationship between screen enrichment and synergistic effect. SAMBA z-scores were plotted against synergy scores for each gene pair. Dashed lines indicate FDR-adjusted P value, q < 0.05, for epistasis and SAMBA results. d, Scatter plot of observed DKO SAMBA scores versus expected SAMBA scores based on the additive effects of the corresponding SKOs for each gene pair (SKO1 + SKO2). Points are colored by synergy score. Linear regression yielded R2 = 0.0152 (n = 2,485 gene pairs; 71 SKO genes), indicating minimal predictability of DKO outcomes from SKO additivity. e, Quantification of indel frequencies in DKO-edited CAR-T cells 5 days after electroporation across three independent batches. P values were calculated using unpaired two-sided t-tests. Data are mean ± s.e.m.; n = 3 human donors. Each dot represents one human donor. f, Quantification of indel frequencies in CAR-T cells from three donors generated across three independent batches 90 days after gene editing. P values were calculated using one-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s multiple-comparisons test versus GTC. Data are mean + s.e.m.; n = 3 independent donor-derived CAR-T cell preparations, generated from three donors in independent batches. NS, not significant, *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001, ****P < 0.0001.

a, Quantification of live cells 5 days after editing in different DKO CAR-T cells compared with controls, n = 3 infection replicates per group. b, Schematic of generation of DKO CAR-T or CAR-Jurkat cell generation and downstream assays. a, Schematic of the time-series RNA-seq experiment in DKO, NR4A1 SKO, SOCS3 SKO, and GTC CAR-T cells undergoing repeated tumour challenges. b, Principal components analysis (PCA) of all RNA-seq samples across all stimulation time-points (left) or separated by timepoint (right). The first two principal components are shown. Genotypes are indicated by dot color, and samples are grouped by time point (left) or genotype (right) using convex hulls. c, Volcano plots of differential expression (DE) analysis for epistasis at each time-point. Significant epistatic transcripts were defined by an FDR-adjusted P value (q value) <0.05 and an absolute log2 fold change (LFC) > 0.5 for the DKO interaction term in the statistical model (Methods). Top DE transcripts are labeled based on significance and LFC, with selected transcripts shown in bold. d, Heatmaps and pathway analysis of DE transcripts from pairwise comparisons between genotypes across stimulation times. For each time point, DE transcripts were hierarchically clustered and shown as heatmaps (left). Pathway analyses were performed independently for each transcript cluster using over-representation analysis (ORA) tests with MSIGDB v7.4 Hallmark gene-sets. Significant pathways (q < 0.05; up to four pathways per cluster shown) are shown on the right, color-coded by the transcript clusters. Dot-size indicates the percentage of pathway genes that were significantly differentially expressed. e, Heatmaps of DE transcripts significantly enriched as NF-κB and STAT5B targets by transcription factor (TF) over-representation analysis (ORA). TF analysis was performed using MSIGDB v7.4 TF gene-sets; ontology names are shown above the heatmaps. f-g, Representative flow cytometry histogram and quantification of p-STAT3 and p-STAT5 in CAR-T cell groups. n = 4 (f), and n = 3 (g) biological replicates per group. h, Representative flow cytometry histograms and quantification of BAX expression in CAR-T cells. n = 3 biological replicates per group. Data in f-h are mean + s.e.m. Significance levels in f-h were calculated using one-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s multiple-comparisons versus GTC (f-g) or DKO (h). Exact P values and detailed statistics are provided in the Source Data. NS, not significant, *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001, ****P < 0.0001.

a, Schematic of the single-cell transcriptomics (SCT) data processing pipeline. b, UMAP projections showing the T cell filtering step in the SCT analysis. B cells were identified by CD20 expression, and T cells were identified by CD3E expression. c, Dot plot showing gene signatures used for immune subset classification. Cells were classified into major immune cell categories, CD8+ T cell subsets and phenotypic states. Dot color and size indicate average gene signature z-score and percentage of expressing cells. Gene-sets used for each gene signature of the dot plot are shown in the right panel tables. d, Dot plot showing transcriptional patterns of marker genes used to classify in vivo CAR-T cell subsets in the SCT data. Dot color and size indicate average gene expression z-score and percentage of expressing cells. e, Distribution of ungrouped T cell subsets across genotypes, shown as stacked bar plots (left) and quantified by subset (right). Cells from mice within each treatment group were pooled before single-cell RNA sequencing. Statistical comparisons of cell-subset proportions between genotypes were performed using two-sided pairwise Fisher’s exact tests with Holm adjustment for multiple comparisons. *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001, ****P < 0.0001. f, Dot plot showing transcriptional patterns for genes comprising signatures of key T cell signaling pathways and functions. Dot color and size indicate average gene expression z-score and percentage of expressing cells, respectively. Data are arranged by hierarchical clustering using the ward.D2 method, and dashed boxes mark DKO subsets.

a, PCA projections of in vivo CAR-T cells grouped by genotype and subset, based on gene expression patterns for each gene-set. PCA was performed using the gene expression data shown in Extended Data Fig. 7f. Points are color-coded by genotype, and polygons mark DKO subset points that clustered together. b, Volcano plots of differential transcription factor signature analysis between DKO and GTC genotypes. Upregulated and downregulated signatures, defined by adjusted P < 0.01 and absolute log2 fold change > 0.25, are shown as red and blue dots, respectively. Statistical comparisons were performed using cell-level Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, and P values were adjusted for multiple testing using Bonferroni correction. c, Dot plot showing transcriptional patterns for genes comprising transcription factor signatures. Dot color and size indicate average gene expression z-score and percentage of expressing cells. Data are arranged by hierarchical clustering using the ward.D2 method, and dashed boxes mark DKO subsets. d, PCA projection of in vivo CAR-T cells grouped by genotype and subset, based on gene expression patterns for each gene-set. PCA was performed using the gene expression data shown in c. Points are color-coded by genotype, and polygons mark DKO subset points that clustered together. e, Left, representative flow cytometry MitoTracker Green signal. Right, quantification of MitoTracker Green MFI; n = 4 per group. CAR-T cells were stimulated with U87-GL-EGFRvIII cells at E:T = 1:1 and cultured for 7 days. f, Left, OCR curves from Seahorse assays. Right, quantification of SRC and MRC; n = 3 per group. g, Illustration of epistasis involving PGC-1α downstream of NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO. Data in f left are mean ± s.e.m., in e,f right are mean +s.e.m. Significance levels were calculated using one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s multiple-comparisons test (e) or two-way ANOVA with Tukey’s multiple-comparisons test (f). n indicates biologically independent samples. CAR-T cells were generated using human donor cells independent of those used in the screen. Exact P values and detailed statistics are provided in the Source Data. *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001, ****P < 0.0001. OCR, oxygen consumption rate; SRC, spare respiratory capacity; MRC, maximal respiratory capacity.
